channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold price dodges CPI shock as US yields hand bulls lifeline
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price bounces off daily lows beneath $4,300 on Friday and reclaims the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of $4,335 following the release of US inflation data, which fueled speculation that a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike next week is almost certain.

item.title: British Pound shakes off US CPI jolt as UK growth steals spotlight
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) climbs slightly against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, up 0.10%, as the latest US consumer inflation report came in line with forecasts, and although money markets have increased the odds of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike next week, traders faded the initial reaction.

item.title: ECB rate hike gives Euro little to work with as Pound holds firm
item.description: EUR/GBP is easing on Friday and slipping toward the 0.8580 area. The cross had pushed to the top of its recent range in the high 0.8590s before running out of steam.

item.title: Silver erases post-CPI slump, rebounds from three-week low
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rebounds sharply on Friday, trading around $64.30 at the time of writing, up 1.13% on the day. The white metal recovers after briefly falling to a three-week low of $62.94 in the immediate reaction to the latest United States (US) inflation figures.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average rallies all session as long yields back off
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just beneath 52,600, roughly 510 points higher, after four sessions of losses. The inflation print was worth about 100 points at 12:30 GMT, and the rest of the advance arrived in the afternoon once the long end of the Treasury curve turned.

item.title: Gold rebounds but Fed rate hike bets risks remain a headwind
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds on Friday, reversing most of the previous day’s losses as a pullback in the US Dollar, US Treasury yields and Oil prices supports the precious metal.

item.title: WTI Oil Price Forecast: corrects lower after reaching overbought levels
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil comes under heavy selling pressure on Friday as traders lock in profits following a sharp rally that pushed the US benchmark to its highest level since May 21. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $96.50, down roughly 4% on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds firm as hotter US inflation fails to cement Greenback's advantage
item.description: AUD/USD is edging higher today but is yet to retake the 0.7200 mark on Friday. The pair is clawing back part of the previous session's sharp sell-off after hitting multi-month highs in the high 0.7200s.

item.title: China: Exports support output as property drags – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research forecasts an improvement in China’s industrial production to 5.0% year-on-year in August, helped by strong export growth driven by AI-related electronics.

item.title: Taiwan: AI boom sustains trade surplus – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank economists, led by Dr. Henry Hao and colleagues, note Taiwan’s August trade surplus hit a record USD22.3bn, driven by strong AI-related exports. Electronics and semiconductor shipments surged, lifting overall exports and imports.

item.title: Japan: BoJ tightening path in focus – ING
item.description: ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song expect the Bank of Japan to raise its policy rate by 25bp to 1.25%, citing persistent price pressures. They project two further 25bp hikes in January and April 2027, taking the rate to 1.75%.

item.title: Swiss Franc struggles even as US Dollar gives back CPI-led gains
item.description: USD/CHF holds onto gains on Friday even as the US Dollar (USD) turns lower following the release of the latest United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, which strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates next week.

item.title: India: Inflation pressures point to tighter bias – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research expects India’s inflation to accelerate to 4.9% year-on-year, with food and energy costs driving a gradual broadening of price pressures.

item.title: Canadian Dollar slides with Oil prices, US CPI fails to keep US Dollar higher
item.description: USD/CAD rises 0.27% on Friday and trades around 1.3870 at the time of writing, after reaching a daily high of 1.3882 in the immediate reaction to the release of United States (US) inflation data.

item.title: United Kingdom: Growth outlook strengthens with AI-driven services – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Chief UK Economist Sanjay Raja highlights stronger-than-expected UK GDP data, with July output rising 0.4% month-on-month and broad-based gains across services, production and construction.

item.title: US UoM Consumer Sentiment Index is seen at 47.8 in September
item.description: American consumer confidence is expected to lose some traction in September, as households have been growing more pessimistic about current conditions and the broader economic outlook, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish stance leaves PLN vulnerable against Euro – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes that the National Bank of Poland maintained a dovish stance, signalling no need to adjust rates potentially until mid-next year despite rising inflation.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish rate path supports Euro – UOB
item.description: UOB economist Lee Sue Ann notes that the European Central Bank (ECB) delivered a widely expected 25 bps hike but signalled a more hawkish stance as inflation risks from the Middle East-driven energy shock remain elevated.

item.title: Bank of Japan: Hawkish hike prospects grow – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research analysts Taimur Baig and Chang Wei Liang expect the Bank of Japan (BoJ) to hike rates by 25 bps at its September 17–18 meeting, citing solid Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth, stronger wages and inflation near the 2% target.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens as US inflation fails to sustain Dollar rebound
item.description: USD/JPY falls 0.54% on Friday and trades around 153.60 at the time of writing.

item.title: Euro steadies against US Dollar after volatile reaction to US CPI
item.description: EUR/USD reverses earlier losses on Friday after the latest United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) report came broadly in line with expectations and failed to trigger a strong market reaction.

item.title: Oil: Gradual easing as dark transits grow – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank strategists argue that Brent crude should gradually retreat toward pre-war levels as covert tanker “dark transits” and diversions restore Gulf supply.

item.title: Breaking: US CPI inflation stays unchanged at 3.4% in August as anticipated
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), held steady at 3.4% in August, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Friday. This print came in line with the market expectation.

item.title: WTI drops more than 4% below $97 as profit-taking kicks in, Iran tensions limit losses
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil drops 4.54% on Friday and trades around $96.00 at the time of writing.

item.title: Euro: ECB hawkish path supports pair – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD is trading heavy around 1.1600 after a hawkish 25 bps European Central Bank (ECB) hike to 2.50%. President Lagarde called the move a “no brainer” and signaled more hikes as inflation is seen above target for an extended period.

item.title: US Dollar: Strength builds on yields – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that the Dollar is benefiting as global bond yields and Oil prices rise, with the USD re-establishing a positive correlation with long-end US yields.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Neutral bias holds as 0.8600 caps the upside
item.description: EUR/GBP edges lower on Friday, drifting toward the lower end of the range seen over the past week.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Yield pressure risks fresh losses against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong highlights a rebound in USD/JPY as higher US Treasury yields, stronger US Dollar (USD) and elevated Oil prices support the pair, even as expectations for further BOJ normalisation cap upside.

item.title: Indian Rupee cracks this week amid higher oil prices, US bond yields
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends its downward spiral against the US Dollar (USD) for the fourth trading day on Friday, with the USD/INR pair rising to near 95.80.

item.title: Euro retreats below 1.1600, Dollar appreciates heading into the US CPI release
item.description: The Euro (EUR) accelerates its reversal against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, as the impulse from a hawkish hike by the European Central Bank (ECB) fades.
